diff.title: Walk through a change
diff.description: Narrated walkthrough of a commit range, a branch or the working tree.

args.target: What to cover: a commit range such as main..HEAD, a branch name, or "the working tree".

diff.template: Make a narrated showntell walkthrough of the changes in {target}. Read the diff with git first and work out what changed and why. Open with the purpose of the change, go through the edits that matter in the order a reviewer needs them, and close with consequences: risks, follow-up work and how to test it. Show code read from disk with `diff file=... rev=...` or `file=` and `lines=` blocks rather than retyping it. Skip renames and formatting unless they matter. Share the link with me as soon as it is playable.

file.title: Walk through a file
file.description: Narrated walkthrough of one source file.

args.path: Path of the file, relative to the project root.

file.template: Make a narrated showntell walkthrough of {path}. Read the file first. Start with what it is for and where it fits in the project, then go through its main parts in the order a newcomer needs them, and end with how it is used and what to watch out for. Show code from disk with `file={path}` and `lines=` ranges, and point at the lines you talk about. Share the link with me as soon as it is playable.

topic.title: Walk through a topic
topic.description: Narrated walkthrough of a concept, algorithm, design or piece of maths.

args.topic: The concept, algorithm, architecture or question to cover.

topic.template: Make a narrated showntell walkthrough of {topic}. Go from the problem it solves, to how it works, to its consequences and trade-offs. Use diagrams, formulas, tables or short code examples where they help, and tie it to code in this project when there is a real example, read from disk. Share the link with me as soon as it is playable.
